shared_elements: carved stone surface in low relief
rounded/oval cartouche-like motifs with interior detail
vertically stacked repeated motifs (column-like arrangement on B's upper zone)
justification: Both are weathered stone bearing shallow relief motifs built from rounded, cartouche-like forms with interior detail, and both include a distinct circular/disc element, with B's upper zone showing a vertical stacking faintly recalling A's columns. The decisive difference is that A is a flat rectangular slab covered edge to edge by a strict orthogonal grid of equally sized sign blocks, whereas B is a massive three-dimensional anthropomorphic figure whose sparse motifs are distributed over a body and head, so composition, format and carving technique differ fundamentally.
